title: Correlation between medial olivocochlear Reflex and speech-in-noise recognition
summary:
It can often be difficult to follow a conversation in a noisy environment. Our brain has a natural mechanism that may help us understand speech even when there is a lot of background noise. In this study, we want to find out whether this mechanism is related to how well people understand speech in noisy situations.
We will measure a natural reflex in the hearing system and brain. We will also test how well you can understand speech while background noise is played at the same time. This will help us find out whether there is a connection between the reflex and how well speech can be understood in noise.
conditions: The subject of the study is speech understanding in noisy everyday situations in young adults with normal hearing. There is no specific underlying health problem.

interventions.name: The participants will undergo a single examination. The following procedures will be performed exclusively for study purposes: pure-tone audiometry, tympanometry, measurement of the stapedius reflex threshold, speech recognition testing using the Göttinger Sentence Test, and measurement of transient

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
No subjective hearing loss, tinnitus, otorrhea, otalgia, vertigo, use of ototoxic medications, or family history of childhood-onset hearing loss.
Exclusion criteria:
Air-conduction hearing threshold >20 dB HL, no measurable TEOAEs, stapedius reflex threshold >95 dB HL, pathological tympanogram.
